title: Color
summary: A colour field: a swatch, the value and a chevron that open the Framework's own compact window -- the static palette first, the product's own colours, recent own colours and «Своё» (shade area, eyedropper, hue and alpha strips, a code in Hex, RGB, HSL or HSB) -- and a way back to an inherited colour. The value is a palette name or a code. Built as a general part because a colour is set in a theme, in a site look, on a label and on a chart series, not only on a record.

root-class.description: Classes added to the root element the component draws.

root-style.description: Inline style declarations set on the root element the component draws, custom properties included.

size.description: The size ladder step, so a colour beside a text field lines up with it.

appearance.description: How the swatch in the field is bounded: bordered (the hairline of outline-variant), outlined (the field's stronger outline) or plain (no border). The paint stays inside the border, so the three looks differ (CO-06).

variant.description: What the control is. field: a field of the control ladder -- the swatch, the value and a chevron -- that opens the Framework's own colour window. theme: only a circle of the current colour, as a site header holds it (C84); it opens the same window at its normal size, with no text and no theme row. brand: the field, for a settings screen («Оформление», C84), with what a person should know about the colour as lines under it (core themeChecks). theme and brand are the brand colour: they rebuild the theme from the colour while it moves (SF.ThemePalette: the four dynamic palettes, never a status, and the brand fill --sf-brand, --sf-on-brand of a header and a cover) on target, committing it when a colour is chosen. Their value is always a code and takes no alpha.

target.description: variant theme or brand: a CSS selector of the element the theme is put on, as inline variables (a settings screen's preview, so the admin keeps its own colours); empty, the document's root. A selector that names nothing puts the theme nowhere.

swatches.description: The colours a product already has, comma separated, each #hex, #hex|Name or a palette name (blue|Name); a name may hold spaces. A piece without a name may list several colours by spaces. They are the first row of the window's palette view, so a person picks the brand colour rather than matching a hex by eye.

palette.description: Whether the window's palette view shows the sixteen hues of the static palette (C17). A hue is stored by its name (blue), the same in every language; the field shows the translated word and the theme picks the tone (50 light, 70 dark). palette="false": only the product's swatches, or «Своё» alone.

custom.description: Whether the window offers «Своё», an own colour: the shade area, the eyedropper where the browser has one, the hue strip and the code row «format | code». custom="false" keeps the palette only (task labels, chart series). Without a palette «Своё» is always offered.

alpha.description: Whether an own colour may be translucent: the alpha strip and the % field are drawn and the value may be #rrggbbaa. Without it a translucent code keeps its colour and drops the alpha, and translucent recent colours are not shown.

clearable.description: Whether a chosen colour can be returned to the inherited one. With variant theme: a second button takes the theme back to what the page had before the control changed it (the Framework colour unless the page set its own).

name.description: The form name. A hidden input carries the value under it, empty while the inherited colour applies.

label.description: The field's label, drawn above the row as sf-input's label and naming the colour input (1.6.0). For a name without a visible label, write aria-label.

choose-label.description: The words on the swatch. Unset, the component answers in the page's language ("Choose a colour" in English).

clear-label.description: The words on the control that returns to the inherited colour. Unset, it follows the page's language; with variant theme the default is the theme words ("Use the original theme colour").

value.description: The colour: a palette name (red, orange, amber, yellow, lime, green, teal, cyan, sky, blue, indigo, violet, purple, pink, brown, gray), stored the same in every language, or the code of an own colour, #rrggbb (or #rrggbbaa with alpha; #rgb and #rgba are read and stored long, lowercase). Empty means nothing is chosen and the inherited colour applies. variants theme and brand store a code.

inherited-value.description: The colour that applies while nothing is chosen. Shown as inherited rather than drawn as the value: a control that drew it as the value would make «not set» and «set to the same colour» look identical, and only one of them follows the theme when the theme changes.

inherited-text.description: What is read in place of a value while nothing is chosen. Unset, it follows the page's language.

reset-label.description: The accessible name of the button that returns to the inherited colour; `clear-label` still names it. Unset, it follows the page's language («Reset to inherited», «Сбросить к наследуемому»).

clear.summary: Return to the inherited colour; the same as setValue(""). Returns whether it changed.

setValue.summary: Set and commit the colour as a person would: normalised, reflected to value, input and then change dispatched when it differs from the committed one. Returns whether the value changed.

resetToInherited.summary: Returns the field to its inherited value, as the reset button does: fires the cancellable sf-field-reset, then empties the own value and focuses the control. Returns whether it was reset (false without an inherited value, without an own value, while disabled or readonly, or when the event was prevented).

openPicker.summary: Opens the colour window on the view the value comes from, or on {view: 'palette' | 'own'}. {anchor} places it against an element of the page and gives focus back to it on close (a settings menu row, C85), instead of the field. Returns whether it is open (false while disabled).

closePicker.summary: Closes the colour window and returns focus to the trigger unless {restoreFocus: false}. Returns true.

change.summary: A colour was committed: once when a swatch is chosen, a drag across the shade area or a strip is released, the code field is left or Enter pressed, a key on a strip rests, or clear is pressed -- not on every step of a drag. Carries the value and the form name; an empty value means the inherited colour applies again. With variant theme or brand and a value, it also carries the theme, its variables (the four palettes and the brand fill), its CSS as a :root rule and its checks -- the names sf-theme-generator's events carried.

input.summary: The colour moved: on every step of a drag across the shade area or a strip, on each key in the code field that reads as a colour, and before each change. Carries the value and the form name. With variant theme or brand, the theme, variables, css and checks as change carries them.

sf-field-reset.summary: The person pressed the reset back to the inherited value. The event of the trait field-inherit@1: one name for every field of the family, so a form hears them all at once and tells them apart by detail.tag. Fired before the field is emptied and cancellable: preventDefault keeps the value. When it is not prevented the field empties, says so with its ordinary change, shows the inherited value again and takes focus back.

tag.description: The element that was reset, as a tag name.

value.description: The field's own value before the reset.

inheritedValue.description: The inherited value it returns to.

name.description: The form name, empty when the field has none.

sf-field:reset.summary: The person pressed the reset back to the inherited value. Fired before the field is emptied and cancellable: preventDefault keeps the value. When it is not prevented the field empties, says so with its ordinary change, shows the inherited value again and takes focus back.

value.description: The field's own value before the reset.

inheritedValue.description: The inherited value it returns to.

name.description: The form name, empty when the field has none.

accessibility.focus: The field's trigger takes focus and keeps a visible focus ring on the frame; it names the field and the colour («Цвет метки: Синий») and says aria-haspopup dialog and aria-expanded. The window is a labelled dialog: focus goes to the chosen swatch (or the shade area in «Своё»), each swatch group is a radio group with one tab stop and arrow keys, the shade area and the strips are sliders with aria-valuetext, Escape closes the window and focus returns to the trigger. After a reset back to the inherited value, focus returns to the trigger; while the value is inherited, the trigger carries it as aria-description and the visible marker is aria-hidden.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-input-color wherever a colour is set -- a theme, a site look, a label, a chart series -- and especially when the colour may be left unset to inherit one. For labels and chart series keep the palette name (custom="false"), so the colour follows the dark theme.
do_not: Do not draw the inherited colour as the value: pass it as inherited-value so «not set» stays distinguishable
Do not listen to input for saving; save on change, which fires once per committed colour
Do not turn a palette name into a hex before storing it: the name follows the theme, the hex does not
Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-input-color label="Brand colour" clearable inherited-value="blue" swatches="#1f6feb|Brand blue, red|Alert"></sf-input-color>
